title: Factors and Factor Pairs Word Problems
intro: Teach factor pairs by arranging a fixed collection into complete rows.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Make different arrays without adding or removing counters. Record each row size and its matching number of rows.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

1 row of 12
1 × 12 = 12
2 rows of 6
2 × 6 = 12
3 rows of 4
3 × 4 = 12

Turn each arrangement to see 12 rows of 1, 6 rows of 2, and 4 rows of 3.

Possible counts per row: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12

These are six possible row sizes. There are three factor pairs when reversed pairs are counted only once.

Ask your student

How do we know we have found every factor pair?

If your student needs help

If a proposed factor leaves counters over, check it by making the rows or dividing.
